numerical_failure.observed_behavior: VIF values explode to extremely high numbers (20, 40, 60, 100+) with no real multicollinearity when the design includes transformations such as 1/x and log(x); when 1 - rsquared is floating-point zero the result is inf with a zero-division warning. With standardize=False on badly scaled data, warnings fire and VIFs become unstable.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: VIF values should stay stable and realistic for data without true multicollinearity, with no spurious warnings when standardize=True; with standardize=False on clean data both options should return the same results (assert_allclose with rtol=1e-7).
trigger_conditions: design matrix includes monotonic nonlinear transformations such as 1/x, log(x), 1/y, log(y) producing columns with very different numeric ranges alongside a constant column of 1s
small r_squared in the auxiliary regression so that 1 - rsquared is floating-point zero, giving inf with a zero-division warning
standardize=False used on badly scaled data (warnings and unstable VIFs fire in that case)
oracle_clues: issue #9791 example uses np.random.seed(42), n=500, x1 uniform(10,100), x2 uniform(5,50), x3 uniform(1,20) with log and inverse transforms

PR #9835 adds test_vif_instability in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_influence.py with three cases: standardize=True stable with no warnings, standardize=False on bad data warns and breaks, and both options agree on clean data
test asserts assert_allclose(vif_true, vif_false, rtol=1e-7) for standardize=True vs standardize=False on clean well-conditioned data (100 rows, intercept plus two normal columns)
issue #6251 describes vif=inf with zero division warning versus very large finite values (1e14, 1e20, 1e200) described as numerical noise; no specific expected VIF values are given

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: VIF values of 1e14, 1e20 or 1e200 described as essentially collinear numerical noise; a small ridge_factor may make VIF very large but finite instead of inf
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-7 in the test comparing standardize=True and standardize=False VIF on clean well-conditioned data
category_specific_evidence: Test asserts assert_allclose(vif_true, vif_false, rtol=1e-7) for variance_inflation_factor with standardize=True vs standardize=False on clean, well-conditioned data (100 rows, intercept plus two normal columns)
Issue #6251 states the current formula vif = 1/(1 - r_squared_i) gives exact zero denominator for small r_squared, producing inf with a zero-division warning
Issue #6251 proposes using ssr/tss instead of (1-rsquared) so the denominator is floating point near zero rather than near one, yielding very large finite VIF values instead of inf
Fix per PR #9835 clips r_sq before computing 1/(1-r_sq), adds standardization and a conditioning warning
Commit and PR titled 'Fix VIF numerical instability by standardizing design matrix', closes #9791
Signature change adds standardize=True keyword to variance_inflation_factor(exog, exog_idx), with a review request to make it keyword-only
